_comment: Poll Calibration: Merdeka Center's published survey results, transcribed by
hand (issue #10). Merdeka Center publishes PDFs and has no API, so a new
report is added here by a person reading it — see docs/poll-calibration.md
for the process, and ADR 0004 for why leader approval is the signal used.
Every number under leader_ratings is copied verbatim from the report and is
never adjusted, rebased or interpolated. `satisfied` and `dissatisfied` are
the published percentages; they need not sum to 100 because the report also
`coalition` is the Coalition the leader's party belonged to DURING the
fieldwork window, and is recorded here rather than derived from
coalitions.json because it is a historical fact about the poll: a later
realignment must not retroactively re-attribute a survey already taken.
A leader with no Coalition at fieldwork time carries null and is reported
as unattributed rather than guessed at — absence of evidence, not evidence
of neutrality, the same rule the Sentiment aggregate follows.
Reports are keyed on fieldwork_end, so re-ingesting one corrects it rather
than storing a second answer for the same survey.

reports.title: Perceptions Towards Economy, Leadership & Current Issues (March 2026)

leader_ratings.note: The report names him only by a former post, 'ex-Chief of UMNO Youth'. He was expelled from UMNO in January 2023 and readmitted on 17 April 2026, after this fieldwork closed on 9 April, so he belonged to no Coalition while the survey ran.

The report names him only as 'former Minister of Economy'. He was still a PKR member throughout the fieldwork window and left the party on 17 May 2026, five weeks after it closed, so this rating is PH's.
